body:
Closes discussion #578.

## Problem

Requested as "octal numbering: e0.0 up to e0.7, then e1.0 to e1.7" — a two-segment counter where the second segment wraps every N values and carries into the first, the same pattern as PLC/rack-style addressing (`module.channel`, 8 channels per card). As the discussion notes, `NumStrategy::nextNumber()` — the shared increment logic every existing numeric part (`unit`/`ten`/`hundred`) calls — does `value + increase` unconditionally: there is no modulus, wraparound, or carry anywhere in the engine today, for any base.

## Change

A configurable **wrap-at-N** counter type rather than a one-off octal mode — N=8 covers the requested case, but the same mechanism covers any wrap-at-N convention at no extra cost:

- New `WrapNum` strategy (`sources/autoNum/numerotationcontextcommands.{h,cpp}`), stored alongside the existing `value`/`increase`/`initialvalue` fields with an added `modulus`. Its own `next()`/`previous()` only wraps its own value — it has no visibility into adjacent parts.
- The real change, as flagged in the discussion: `NumerotationContextCommands::next()`/`previous()` gained `carry()`/`borrow()` — when a wrap part's own `next()` would reach/exceed its modulus (or go below 0 on `previous()`), the nearest preceding *numeric* part is bumped by exactly one unit, skipping non-numeric parts (e.g. a literal `.` separator) along the way. Wrap parts chain correctly if placed adjacently (e.g. seconds → minutes → hours).
- `NumerotationContext` gained a 5th pipe-separated field (`modulus`, default `0` = non-wrapping) in its serialized form, persisted as a `modulus` XML attribute the same way `initialvalue` is already persisted for `unitfolio`/`tenfolio`/`hundredfolio`.
- New "Cyclique (modulo)" entry in the part-type dropdown (`numparteditorw`), available for element, conductor, and folio autonumbering alike — all three already go through `NumerotationContextCommands`.

**One design detail surfaced by testing, not called out in the original discussion**: for the leading part of a wrap-and-carry pair to actually stay fixed except when carried into (producing `e0.0...e0.7, e1.0...` rather than advancing on every step under its own strategy), its own `increase` must be `0`. The increase spinbox's minimum was hardcoded to `1`, which made this configuration impossible through the UI regardless of the engine supporting it — lowered to `0` and documented with a tooltip, since it isn't obvious from the UI alone that a "static" digit is how you compose wrap-and-carry.

## Testing

Built clean (no new warnings). Verified in the running app via the numbering config dialog's own Suivant/Précédent buttons, which call the production `NumerotationContextCommands::next()`/`previous()` directly (not a test double): a two-part context — `unit` (increase=0) + `wrap` (mod 8) — produced exactly `e0.0 → ... → e0.7 → e1.0 → ... → e1.7` over 15 "next" clicks, and the exact reverse with correct borrowing over the following "previous" clicks.

commits.messageBody:
Adds a configurable wrap-at-N counter type to the autonumbering engine
(NumerotationContext + NumerotationContextCommands), covering PLC/rack-style
addressing conventions like "e0.0...e0.7, e1.0...e1.7" (8 channels per
card) generally, rather than hardcoding octal specifically.

- New "wrap" part type (WrapNum, alongside the existing UnitNum/TenNum/
  HundredNum strategies) stores a modulus in addition to the existing
  value/increase/initialvalue fields. Its own next()/previous() only wraps
  its own value modulo the configured modulus -- carrying into (or
  borrowing from) the adjacent part requires visibility across parts,
  which only the composition loop has.
- NumerotationContextCommands::next()/previous() gained carry()/borrow()
  helpers: when a wrap part's own next() would reach/exceed its modulus
  (or go below 0 on previous()), the nearest preceding numeric part is
  bumped by exactly one unit, skipping non-numeric parts (e.g. a "."
  string separator). Wrap parts chain correctly if adjacent (e.g. seconds
  wrapping into minutes wrapping into hours).
- For the leading part of a wrap-and-carry pair to stay fixed except when
  carried into (i.e. actually produce "e0.0...e0.7, e1.0..." rather than
  advancing on every step under its own strategy), its own increase must
  be 0. The increase spinbox's minimum was 1, which made this
  configuration impossible through the UI -- lowered to 0 and documented
  with a tooltip, since this wasn't obvious from the UI alone.
- NumerotationContext gained a 5th pipe-separated field (modulus) in its
  serialized string form, defaulting to 0 (non-wrapping) for every
  existing part type; toXml()/fromXml() persist it as a "modulus" XML
  attribute the same way "initialvalue" is already persisted for
  unitfolio/tenfolio/hundredfolio.
- New "Cyclique (modulo)" entry in the part-type dropdown (numparteditorw),
  available for element, conductor, and folio autonumbering alike, since
  all three already go through NumerotationContextCommands.

Verified in the running app via the numbering config dialog's own
Suivant/Précédent buttons (which call the production
NumerotationContextCommands::next()/previous() directly): a two-part
context (unit, increase=0 + wrap mod 8) produced exactly
e0.0→...→e0.7→e1.0→...→e1.7 on repeated "next", and the exact reverse
(with correct borrowing) on repeated "previous".

title: Add wrap-and-carry (cyclic/modulo) auto-numbering
